name: DR Congo
summary_text: DR Congo is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex conduct has never been criminalised — but the reality on the ground is severe insecurity: mob justice against perceived LGBT people is documented, police extortion is routine, the east is an active conflict zone (M23), and LGBT organisations (Savie asbl in Bukavu) report systematic violations in their 2024 UPR submission. There is no legal gender recognition and no protection infrastructure; Kinshasa's small scene is underground. For a visitor: no statutory exposure, but outing risks mob violence with no effective state protection anywhere in the country.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA World Database jurisdiction page for DR Congo: documents legal status for same-sex conduct and gender recognition.

Stakeholder submission to the DRC's 5th-cycle UPR (March 2024) by Savie asbl NGO and others: the DRC does not criminalise same-sex relations but neither protects nor promotes LGBTIQ+ rights; public displays of same-sex affection can be prosecuted under indecent-exposure provisions (Article 176 of the Penal Code: 'anyone who publicly outrages morals by actions...').

sources.title: DR Congo: Rebels Were Recruited to Crush Protests | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Dec 2017): 'DR Congo: Rebels Were Recruited to Crush Protests' — child soldiers reportedly recruited by a militia to suppress opposition demonstrations; general human-rights context for the security environment, not LGBT-specific.

GayOut travel guide for DR Congo: rates the country 'High Risk for LGBTQ+' - no explicit national criminalisation but Article 176 ('indecent acts') and local ordinances applied to LGBTQ people; armed militia groups in eastern DRC have committed extreme violence against LGBTQ people with near-total impunity; state authority collapse means legal protections are theoretical.

Wikiwand (Wikipedia mirror) on LGBTQ rights in the DRC: same-sex activity legal for both sexes (never outlawed, even under Belgian rule), equal age of consent; but no gender-identity recognition, no relationship recognition (same-sex marriage banned constitutionally since 2006), limited protections; church groups promote the view that homosexuality is immoral; public same-sex affection can trigger prosecution under indecency provisions.

sources.title: LGBT Rights In Congo: Everything You Should Know Before You Visit! 🇨🇩
sources.claim_summary: Queer In The World travel guide: 'LGBT Rights In Congo: Everything You Should Know Before You Visit' - travel-oriented overview of the legal situation and safety considerations for LGBTQ visitors to the DRC.
